results.content: Consumer sentiment plunged in September amid heightened inflation fears, hitting its second-lowest level on record in the University of Michigan’s monthly survey released Friday. The survey’s headline index hit a level of 47.8, down 7.5% from the August reading and off 13.2% from a year ago. This was the second-lowest reading on record for data going back to 1952 — the bottom coming in May as rising prices also jolted the outlook. Indeed, the one-year inflation outlook surged to 4.6%, up 0.6 percentage point from the prior level and the highest since hitting the same level in June.
